chapter: Early bands and joining George Lewis
title: Giving up music in the Depression, then the Hubert Moran band
summary: After the Depression he sold his drums, but sitting in at Wilford Ledet's house led to a Halloween barn job and a six-piece band with Hubert Moran and Walter Nelson.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: And after he had heard me, he told me about joining up with him and Foster Lewis. Him and Foster, what they call him, Foster Stan. But it was Foster Stan and his brother dude had their own band. And so when they got jobs where we used to take off, you know, get off them nights and go play the job and come back and finish our work. So he told me, he gave me good advice. He said, you keep up. He said, you got a little, a little bit to learn yet. So after I got married, well, I had given up music because the depression that came along and things that got so tough. I said, well, I just said, well, to get rid of those set. I said, because they ain't nothing gonna happen for quite a long time. So we moved right across the street from here, right next to the church there, before they built the church up. A friend of mine named Walter Nelson, you done heard him, I'm more sure. Well, yes, I've heard of him.

Yeah, I never knew him. Well, we went up to Wilford's house, Wilford Ledet. He was a drummer. Well, he had a set of drums up there. Well, I wasn't worried about no drum. We was just sitting down and having a good time. And I started to pat my foot and Walter said, you ever played drums before? I said, yeah. I said, why, yeah? He said, well, I noticed you're keeping good time with your foot. I said, yeah, I used to play quite a while. And so Wilford set up his drums and it was him. And I and the guitar. So during that year for Halloween night, Wilford had got a job back in Gentilly. It was in a barn, cow barn. And he asked if I wanted to play the job. I said, well, I don't have no set. He said, well, I'll let you use my set. So it was Hubert Moran on trumpet, Walter Nelson on guitar and me on drums. So after we knocked off that night Hubert Moran told me, he said, Joe, I like your style of playing. So you kind of remind me of Lindsey a little bit. He said, why don't you get your set? And so we come around by your house and give you rehearsals and get you back in the racket again. You can make a little extra change. So I went and bought a secondhand outfit. And well, they used to come over there and hear me, Walter, just them two. And they used to work me out several times a week. And first thing you know, we had six pieces. Well, we started playing all down the country. And then we was playing out here by Joe Chenellis at the Silver Star.
Who else was in the band?
And well, at that time we had him see Walter Moran and this crippled fellow used to play clarinet. How did Walter play?
